LESSON: ASPECTS OF TRADITIONAL CULTURE IN THE COUNTY.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: SOCIAL ORGANIZATIONS Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Lear
Topic 3.1: Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County., part of SOCIAL ORGANIZATIONS Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Lear in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: howcase different aspects of traditional culture in class. Why is culture important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: Learners collect and record aspects of traditional culture practiced in the community.

● Creativity and imagination: Learners ask challenging questions as they discuss in groups the importance of traditional culture in the

County.

● Self-Efficacy: Learners develop effective communication skills as they brainstorm in pairs to identify aspects of traditional culture in the

County (dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, festivals and ceremonies).

30

Values:
● Respect: Learners recognise different aspects of traditional culture in their County.

● Unity: Learners display team spirit as they work in groups to describe aspects of traditional culture in the County.

● Social Justice: Learners accord equal opportunities in sharing responsibilities as they collect and record aspects of traditional culture in

the community. (pictures, songs, artefacts, dress, food, paintings, tools).

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self Esteem: Learners are able to accept and like self as they discuss in groups the importance of traditional culture in the County.

● Self-Awareness: Learners appreciate individual uniqueness as they work in groups to describe aspects of traditional culture in the

County.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Religious Education: as learners develop communication skills as they discuss in groups the importance of traditional culture in the

County.

Suggested Learning Resources

Artefacts, Realia and Cultural and historic sites
